title: 100% AI dev with just prompts on Claude except for the Art assets. I was surprised how far I could push it before I needed help.
author: WeightNational9457
selftext:
https://beta.potatozzz.com/

Check it out, it's free - I used Claude with Vscode, just prompts. Took me around 3 to 4 weeks (not full time.) I'm pretty amazed at what it can do with just prompts.

Just to be clear I built this for fun, but I showed it to the company I work for and they are picking it up and helping me launch it with support on hosting and potentially other things. But what you see now is the most raw version that was only built with Claude prompts.

comments.author: ul90
comments.body: Nice game., But I think it still needs a lot of fine tuning.

replies.author: WeightNational9457
replies.body: would love to hear your feedback, what are those things?

replies.author: ul90
replies.body:
The enemies are rushing in too fast at the start. New players need a litte bit more time to get used to the controls and the game mechanics. So, the "waves" should be smaller at the beginning and then increase. And a short pause between the waves. I also only saw one wave, but with many enemies.

It's also not clear what the items are for that the enemies lose and you can collect (I think for power-ups, but that's not clear). The power-up/level-up dialog just plops in, what feels a little bit random. Maybe the dialog could be animated and the should be a type of "advance notice" like a power-up bar that is blinking / animated.

Next thing that's a little bit confusing: the walls appear and disappear; I don't understand the logic behind that. Or is this a bug?

replies.author: Atoning_Unifex
replies.body:
1st...great job. It's a good start. I don't like games like this but I too am trying to learn this and I'm interested in other peoples results. 

The enemies hit target is too small.
It would be nice if there was some lateral movement. It's hard to line it up with finger. I keep being almost on and still missing. Have to keep running back and turning 180 degrees around again. Pretty tedious. 
Too many enemies by far at the beginning. Make the 1st few levels pretty easy to avoid discouraging too soon. 
Click to continue button needs to be much more prominent and easy to tap. It's almost hidden at the bottom.

replies.author: WeightNational9457
replies.body:
I used assets that previously existed from my company's marketing/social media mascot and some stuff I got from itch.io some I started drawing myself.

For the HUD and the UI it was all Claude. I found a code pen of a button style I liked (https://codepen.io/svper563/pen/KKrzRaq) and I asked Claude to study the code and recreated it. It took a few prompts, after achieving the style I wanted I asked it to add it to the Md file so that moving forward it refers to that design style.
